Definition: from a derivative of G1672; a Hellenist or Greek-speaking Jew:--Grecian.
BiblicalUsage: A Hellenist was a Greek-speaking Jew, and the early church had to learn how to hold them together with the Hebrews. In Acts 6:1 the Grecians murmur because their widows are neglected, in Acts 9:29 Paul disputes against the Grecians and they go about to slay him, and in Acts 11:20 men of Cyprus and Cyrene preach to the Grecians at Antioch.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the murmuring in Acts 6 is the first church fight, and the answer is the first deacons: the church did not argue the widows away, it appointed men to feed them. That is how a divided church becomes one church.
